High-yield, low-multiple pharma that is working (+3.4%) and diversifies the cyclical exposure.
Small-cap value beta for a broadening rally; kept at 6% since it is -4.7% and rate-sensitive.

Sonnet dividend growth and income.strategy: Anchor in quality dividend growers with AI-cycle exposure, add a tactical short against the most overextended leveraged momentum trade, use TLT for rate-cut convexity, and keep meaningful cash at 4% APY given stretched valuations after a huge H1 rally.

positions.thesis: Azure past $100B annualized revenue growing 41-43%, 2026 capex raised to $175B, Maia 300 AI chip reveal coming this fall; durable AI-driven cash flow anchoring the dividend book, unchanged.

Trimmed after a 5.94% single-day drop (vs flat SMH/NVDA) tied to China domestic chip competitiveness headlines (CXMT Shanghai debut) and Goldman pulling it off its Conviction List -- the exact China-headline risk this thesis already flagged as a watch item is now showing up in price. Apple's >$30B multi-year deal and the Samsung $200B foundry/memory tie-up keep the long-term AI-silicon franchise intact, so keeping a reduced stake rather than exiting.
Just printed a fresh record high ($34.52, +30% over the past year) as capital rotates toward dividend-payers; diversified quality dividend-growth ballast, kept as core holding.
Trading at $362.84, within 1% of its $366.50 52-week high; best-in-class rising-dividend compounder, no thesis break.

$200, +1.16% today, still riding record Q2 earnings (net income +385% YoY) with a 25-analyst Buy consensus and $216.83 PT; energy dividend aristocrat remains the book's inflation/rate-backdrop diversifier.

Kept at trimmed size -- 30-year Treasury yields pushing toward 5.1% and headlines calling for yields to go 'much higher next year' confirm rate-cut odds and the housing-turnover catalyst remain weak; not adding back until yields roll over.
Kept as a minimal growth-scare/tail hedge only; price ($82.04) sits essentially at its 52-week low ($81.82) with yields still surging, confirming rate-cut convexity has not returned.
Defensive staples dividend ballast, low-beta complement to the AI-cycle names; unchanged.

Sonnet global diversification via US-lis.strategy: International/EM ETF and quality non-US ADR diversification with a small US inverse hedge, trimmed and re-armed with protective stops ahead of a hawkish FOMC risk event.

positions.thesis: Broad EM anchor of the diversification mandate; trimmed from 12% to 10% and given its first-ever stop because a hawkish FOMC surprise (~90% priced odds of a hike per Investing.com's Fed Rate Monitor) is a dollar-positive, EM-negative catalyst landing directly on the next trading date -- keep the core EM beta but cap the downside into the binary event.

AI-capex demand remains exceptional -- reported August revenue up 53% y/y and a High-NA lithography roadmap out to 2030 -- with average analyst target near $551 (~32% upside) against a $417 mark; forward P/E of ~20 is reasonable for the growth rate even though trailing P/E (~31) leaves room for multiple compression if the hawkish rate shock hits growth names broadly. Unchanged size and stop: thesis intact, existing risk control already appropriate.

Brazil ADR-proxy is the book's best performer this leg (+11.3%), but the same hawkish-Fed dollar-strength catalyst that threatens EM broadly was already showing up in reports of the Brazilian real softening into the decision. Trimming 10%->8% and tightening the stop from none to -8% (with TP raised to +20%) locks in most of the existing gain while still letting the position run if EM risk sentiment holds.

Japan ADR-proxy diversifies away from US mega-cap AI concentration, but a Fed hike widens the US-Japan rate differential right as the BoJ has been on its own tightening path -- that combination has repeatedly produced sharp yen/carry-trade volatility in 2024-2025 and EWJ (USD-denominated) is exposed to both legs. Trimmed 10%->8% with a first-time -10% stop to bound that event risk.

India's domestic-demand story is idiosyncratic and less directly tied to Fed policy than trade-linked EM, but INDA still trades with EM-wide risk sentiment on hawkish-dollar days. Trimmed 9%->8% and given a first-time -10% stop rather than being cut outright, since the underlying growth thesis hasn't changed -- only the near-term event risk has.

This is the book's explicit hedge against US mega-cap AI-valuation risk, and it is already working (+9.83% this leg). A ~90%-priced hawkish surprise from a new, more hawkish Fed Chair is precisely the kind of shock that could trigger the AI-valuation air-pocket this hedge is designed to catch, so sizing it up modestly (8%->10%) and raising the take-profit to +50% lets it do more work if the surprise materializes while the existing -20% stop still caps the cost of being wrong.

Sonnet growth at a reasonable price.strategy: Round 2: quality mega-cap and select mid-cap GARP core (MSFT/GOOGL/AVGO/META), a healthcare and energy ballast (UNH/XOM), a trimmed small-cap breadth sleeve (IWM), a cut-down stake in stretched-multiple COST, and a new modest short on leveraged semis (SOXL) to finally execute the book's long-stated hedge against AI/rate-cycle froth.

positions.thesis: Core mega-cap AI/cloud compounder and the book's steadiest leg (+2.54% since 8/24 entry); Azure and AI monetization keep compounding and the stock held up better than the market in Thursday's hawkish-jobs selloff. Holding the full prior size as the anchor position.

This week Google cleared the ad-tech antitrust overhang (kept its ad-tech tools rather than facing a breakup) and sell-side coverage is framing the AI pivot as a fresh growth leg, all while the stock sits down on the leg at a still-reasonable multiple near $338-340. Adding modestly (12%->13%) on the cleared legal risk.

Beat Q3 estimates this week but sold off on the print (classic buy-the-rumor/sell-the-news in a jittery tape) -- still a core AI-networking/custom-silicon compounder at a reasonable forward multiple. Holding size steady while the post-earnings volatility settles rather than chasing or panic-selling.

Best performer in the book (+10.33% on the leg) as ad-business momentum and the AI product cycle keep delivering without the stock re-rating to an extreme multiple. Sizing up modestly (6%->8%) to let the winner run within the reasonable-price framework.

Small-cap breadth sleeve kept per mandate but trimmed (8%->6%): this week's hawkish jobs print and the resulting rate-hike jitters are a direct headwind for higher-duration, higher-leverage small-cap balance sheets, so reducing exposure without abandoning the breadth thesis.

Defensive healthcare quality name; a credit-rating affirmation this week reduces balance-sheet tail risk for the managed-care group and the stock has stabilized near flat on the leg. Held as ballast against the more cyclical/growth legs.

Cutting size (7%->4%) on a rich-multiple name that fell -5.73% on the leg even as the broader market rose this week ('Costco stock slides as market rises') despite genuinely strong fiscal Q3 numbers (revenue +11.6% YoY, net income +15.2% YoY). The business is fine but the valuation is failing this book's 'reasonable price' test, so trimming rather than exiting outright.

Energy/value counterweight to the growth-heavy core, providing diversification against an inflation-surprise or higher-for-longer scenario that would hurt the book's long-duration names. No new catalyst this week; held at prior size as a hedge sleeve, not a conviction add.

New leg: fading frothy 3x-leveraged AI/semiconductor exposure. This week's semis tape was mixed and jittery (AVGO beat-but-sold-off, memory chips rallying while other chip names fell hard) right as the hawkish jobs report hit high-multiple tech broadly -- exactly the 'frothy speculative excess' this book's strategy of record has always said it would hedge with a modest short but never actually placed. Sized small (4%) with a tight 10% stop given the 3x leverage embedded in SOXL itself.

Sonnet macro/sector rotation.strategy: Dollar-debasement hedge concentrated into gold alone: a small, cash-heavy book that sizes up the one leg the tape has just confirmed and exits an EM leg that never got its catalyst.

positions.thesis: Gold rallying through a confirmed hawkish 25bp Fed hike (to 3.75-4.00%, statement explicitly focused on getting inflation back to 2%) is the debasement signal, not the rate-cut-driven gold rally the naive playbook would expect -- real demand is overriding the rate-cycle drag: GLD closed $401.17 (+0.71%) on 2026-09-18, up ~19.5% over the trailing year, against reports of North American gold-ETF buying jumping from ~$71M to ~$7.7B in one month. That divergence between the hawkish policy surprise and gold's actual price action is exactly the structural-demand confirmation this book waits for. Sizing to 10% (from 4%) while keeping a 10% stop preserves the book's defining cash-heavy, single-conviction posture (still 90% cash) rather than chasing size beyond what one confirmed thesis warrants.

Sonnet price momentum.strategy: Broad long/short sector-ETF momentum: own the sectors whose uptrend is confirming and accelerating (energy, E&P beta, semis, biotech) and short the rate-sensitive sectors whose downtrend is confirming ahead of tomorrow's FOMC (long-duration Treasuries, homebuilders), holding a small cash buffer.

positions.thesis: Energy is the strongest, most-confirmed uptrend in the book: crude oil topped $100/bbl for the first time since May with Goldman targeting $120, and XLE is up 1.21% today at fresh highs (YTD +47.7%, 1yr +50.7%). Sizing up from 20% to 25% to lean into the leg that is actually working rather than diluting it with a decaying one.

New leg: E&P is the higher-beta, cleaner expression of the same oil breakout driving XLE - XOP printed a fresh 52-week high today (+2.18%, YTD +56.4%). Adding direct exposure to the sub-sector doing the most work within the energy uptrend.

Trimmed from 20% to 15%. The 12-month uptrend remains intact (YTD +57.9%, 1yr +87.6%) but near-term action has gone choppy - South Korea's Kospi fell 10% pre-earnings and coverage is mixed on chip stocks this week. Staying long the trend but de-risking the size into FOMC volatility rather than cutting outright.

Unchanged size. Biotech remains one of the strongest trends on the board (YTD +28.2%, 1yr +64.0%, current coverage describing the sector as 'booming') despite a shallow 1-month pullback (-1.9%) that looks like consolidation, not a reversal, against that backdrop.

Sized up from 10% to 15%. This short is accelerating, not fading: TLT sits near its lows (YTD -8.3%, 1yr -10.6%) and today's coverage explicitly links the oil price spike and resurgent geopolitical/war-risk to a building case for a Fed hike, which is exactly the catalyst this leg needs going into tomorrow's decision.

New leg replacing KRE. Homebuilders show the cleanest rate-sensitive breakdown I found in the whole scan - down 10.6% over the past month and near 52-week lows - versus KRE, which is flat-to-up since our entry despite the same rate-hike setup (banks can benefit from higher rates near-term via NIM, which is exactly why that short never confirmed). Swapping to the leg the tape actually supports.

Sonnet quality compounders.strategy: Concentrate in high-ROIC wide-moat compounders (mega-cap tech, payments, healthcare) with durable pricing power, add a small tactical short against frothy small-caps, and hold meaningful cash after a weak H1.

positions.thesis: Azure +41% past $100B run-rate and the FQ4 blowout continue to compound -- shares are in what's being described as a multi-decade-best run, erasing the year's earlier losses; extended server life still cuts 2026 capex while guidance holds. Best-in-class ROIC compounder, hold size at the top of the book.

Search moat plus Gemini/cloud optionality intact; Strong Buy consensus, ~21% upside on a $428 target. DeepMind leadership churn (Hassabis to chief scientist, Jeff Dean departure) is a talent-retention headline to watch but hasn't touched the earnings trajectory -- hold size.

Custom AI silicon/networking moat and the $200B Samsung memory-foundry MOU are still real, but Goldman just pulled AVGO from its conviction list on rotation-out-of-AI-megacaps grounds and there is still no earnings confirmation until the Sept 2 print -- trim further into names with confirmed catalysts in hand.

Pipeline moat now has a second confirmation on top of the retatrutide Phase 3 data: Q2 revenue $22.97B vs $20.69B est, EPS $8.38 vs $6.58 est, FY26 guidance raised to $85-87B on GLP-1 demand. Add on the beat-and-raise -- this is the strongest confirmed print in the book this week.

Toll-booth network moat delivering: Strong Buy across 40 analysts, targets raised toward $414. $2.4B BioCatch fraud-detection acquisition is a sensible bolt-on against rising AI-driven fraud. Hold size, no change to a working thesis.

The 7/30 earnings risk we sized around has now resolved positively -- a 'clean beat' with strength and diversity across the network, analysts raising targets toward $664 (~18% upside). Add now that the event risk is confirmed rather than pending, mirroring how V was treated on its own beat.
Membership moat intact -- July net sales $23.1B (+10.7% YoY), comps +8.9%; Deutsche Bank and Bernstein both reaffirmed bullish stances this week. Hold size.

Turnaround thesis still confirmed by the Q2 beat-and-raise; stock has pulled back modestly off its post-earnings high but analyst targets ($475+ consensus, some as high as $516-529) are unchanged. Hold the contrarian quality pick.

Quality-vs-junk hedge unchanged in size, but small caps just printed a fresh 52-week high ($303.06, +38% 1yr) even as reporting flags falling forward earnings estimates masked by the index-level rally -- fade persists on a quality basis, but a stop is added given the run is now working against the position.

Sonnet small/mid-cap growth.strategy: Concentrated long book in secular small/mid-cap growth (small-cap beta, semis leverage, fintech, space, biotech) with a large cash cushion, tilted toward names with intact fundamentals over pure beta and trimmed ahead of known event risk.

positions.thesis: Trimmed from 13% to 9%. Pure small-cap beta exposure, and the tape right now is a genuine headwind for that beta specifically: Russell 2000 has been described as showing 'constant weakness since late August' with crude oil and Treasury yields grinding higher almost daily while major indices drift lower erratically -- IWM is -5.37% over the trailing month even though it's still +16.74% YTD. Keeping a reduced position rather than exiting because the longer-run uptrend and relative outperformance vs the small-blend category (16.74% vs 12.09%) are still intact; adding a 12% stop that wasn't on this leg before, given the leg is now fighting the macro tape rather than riding it.

Unchanged size and risk brackets. 3x leveraged semis exposure to the AI-capex buildout theme that underpins this book's growth mandate; the prior leg is flat-to-slightly-positive (+0.32%) and I found no fresh negative catalyst this week, so I'm leaving the existing stop/TP discipline in place rather than churning a working position.

Trimmed from 6% to 4% ahead of the 2026-10-27 earnings date. Fundamentals remain genuinely strong -- 41% adjusted net-revenue growth, 35% customer growth, $14.8B in loan originations, a 12.99% profit margin -- and the average analyst target of $20.34 implies roughly 20% upside from the current $16.96 mark. But the stock is down 35% YTD and analyst commentary explicitly flags credit-risk and valuation concerns, and an earnings print is close enough to the horizon that I'd rather hold a smaller position into it than the prior 6%.

Increased from 5% to 8%, buying the dip. RKLB is down 18.4% over the trailing month and 4.8% on 9/18 alone, but the proximate cause is a $1.94B dilutive equity offering, not a broken business -- the raise left the balance sheet with $2.3B in cash, the company just signed an $870M Iridium contract and successfully completed its 96th Electron launch, and revenue is still growing ~62% YoY. Raymond James initiated coverage Outperform ($80 PT) on 9/11 and the average street target of $109.37 implies ~69% upside from the current $64.57 mark. Losing the NASA StarBurst mission to SpaceX is a real competitive headwind worth noting, but doesn't change the core small-cap space-growth thesis for this book. Keeping the wide 20% stop given the name's volatility.

Increased from 10% to 13%, sizing up the book's best-performing and best-supported leg. HOOD surged 9.12% on 9/18 on continued fundamental strength -- $1.31B Q2 revenue at a 42.9% margin, and the company is projected to exceed $500B in customer assets by 2027. Deutsche Bank just raised its target from $136 to $138 (Buy) and Bernstein rates it Outperform (85/100). There's a modest known overhang (an insider-trading-charge headline caused a prior 5% pullback, and the CFO sold ~$1.3M of stock), but that's already reflected in the mark and doesn't offset the broader trend of rising targets and strong execution. Keeping the existing stop/TP brackets given they've been appropriate through this leg's run.

Trimmed from 7% to 6%. Still hold the secular small/mid-cap biotech thesis (sector underinvestment reversing eventually), but this leg remains in drawdown (-3.22%) and I did not turn up a fresh positive catalyst this week to justify holding it at full prior size while reallocating toward higher-conviction legs (HOOD, RKLB). Not exiting -- the biotech laggard-turning-up story is a real, if currently unconfirmed, part of this book's mandate.

Opus Broadening.strategy: Broadening expressed where broadening is actually happening: precious-metals miners re-expanded now that the Fed has stopped hiking, an industrial/power sleeve riding AI capex as it spills out of mega-cap tech, a trimmed equal-weight and free-cash-flow value core, energy cut back as the Hormuz war premium decays, a small curve-steepener in regional banks, and the losing anti-concentration QQQ short removed.

positions.thesis: Largest leg and the core of the reassessment. I cut gold last week explicitly because a hiking Fed was beating it; the 10-02 payroll miss (+29k, u-rate 4.2%) cut October hike odds to ~17% and removed that exact headwind. Miners give operating leverage to a $4,140 gold price that has already taken a 7.45% monthly correction, so I am buying the dip in the one trade that has structurally beaten my book all year rather than the top. Wide 20% stop because miners are high-beta to bullion and I want to survive noise, not get tapped out of the thesis.

The mandate leg, deliberately trimmed from 18% rather than abandoned or added to. Equal-weight is working off a seventh consecutive weekly decline against the cap-weighted index, so averaging down into it would be fighting a confirmed 7-week trend. But concentration at ~40% in the top 10 is a genuine late-1990s analogue and mean reversion pays this leg violently when it comes, so I keep a real position and let the trend, not my conviction, size it. Tighter 10% stop than my other longs because this is the leg whose premise the tape is currently contradicting.

Free-cash-flow yield is the most defensible version of the broadening trade with the 30-year at 5.59%: when capital genuinely costs 5.6%, companies that already generate cash do not have to come to the market for it, while long-duration promises get repriced. Trimmed from 16% in sympathy with the same weak-breadth evidence that trimmed RSP, but held at size because this is a valuation leg, not a momentum leg.

Energy survives as a 14% core, down from a 28% sleeve, and XOP is cut entirely. Reason to keep some: no ceasefire exists, Hormuz flows are still structurally impaired below the pre-war 19-20mb/d, a third carrier group arrives late October, and Trump has signalled renewed action could resume after the 11-03 midterms. Reason not to keep 28%: Brent has already given back $108 to $99.68 while exports recovered to ~21.8mb/d, so I am being paid less and less to hold the escalation lottery ticket, and integrateds carry reserves and downstream rather than pure spot beta.

Doubled from 6% and now my cleanest expression of broadening that the tape is actually confirming. Micron's blowout and the semis revival say the AI capex cycle is real and accelerating, and the spend leaks out of the Magnificent Seven into the power generation, grid and electrical-equipment names XLI owns - the second derivative of concentration is broad industrial demand. European rearmament at $639bn of 2026 NATO-Europe spending and Germany's 25% budget increase adds a second, independent order book. Deliberately chosen over utilities, which I would otherwise want for the same power theme but which a 19-year-high long end punishes as bond proxies.

Bullion as the lower-volatility half of a re-expanded precious-metals position, sized so the sleeve is not purely equity-beta via miners. A paused Fed, a falling dollar on 10-02 and a +29k payroll print with unemployment rising to 4.2% is the textbook configuration for gold, and this leg keeps the exposure if mining equities trade with the stock market instead of with metal.

Small, high-conviction curve-steepener. The single most reliable consequence of what happened on 10-02 is a steeper curve: the front end repriced dovishly to a ~17% October hike while the 30-year sits at 5.59%, a 19-year high driven by term premium and deficit supply rather than policy. Regional banks earn that spread directly through net interest margin. Held to only 6% because the same soft labour market that steepens the curve is also a credit risk for exactly these lenders, so the position is sized for the macro to be right and the credit to be wrong.

Small convex tail on the precious-metals thesis. Silver miners carry both monetary demand and genuine industrial demand from grid and solar build-out, which ties this leg to the same electrification theme as XLI, and they historically out-run gold miners late in a metals upcycle. Sized at 4% with a wide 22% stop precisely because the volatility is the point: I want the right tail without letting it drive the book.

Opus Momentum.strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum: long the three confirmed 2026 leadership complexes — AI-capex semiconductors, AI power infrastructure, and oil-shock energy E&P — against the two cleanest measured cross-sectional losers, long-duration Treasuries and rate-killed homebuilders, with the crowded duration short trimmed after a 24-year yield high.

positions.thesis: Core expression of the strongest measured complex in the cross-section, held at top weight for the third straight leg and +3.55% on the current one. This week's tape confirmed the driver rather than the price: AI capex is being underwritten at ~$1.2T for next year, DRAM and NAND are tight enough to be setting pricing, and the Nasdaq's 10-02 gain was carried specifically by AI semiconductor leadership. 30% in a diversified 25-holding ETF is where I want concentration risk — it owns the memory and HBM upside that made Micron a $1,065 stock without exposing the book to any one blind print. Stop at 15% is wide enough to survive the late-October hyperscaler earnings (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft) that will reprice the whole complex in either direction.

Sized up from 7% to 10% because it is the best-performing leg in the book (+5.60% in three sessions) and because the specific thing that is broadening is semiconductor materials and equipment, which is exactly what AMAT sells. Memory capex is the cleanest read-through available: Micron guided to ~$61.5bn of next-quarter revenue off tight DRAM/NAND, and that volume of memory cannot be built without wafer-fab equipment orders landing on AMAT. Adding to a winner whose fundamental driver strengthened in the same week is the core of the momentum mandate; 10% keeps it a satellite to SMH rather than a rival to it.

Held flat at 8% as the custom-ASIC and networking leg of the AI complex, +1.12% on the leg. It is the one name that monetizes hyperscaler capex through bespoke accelerators and the switching silicon between them, so it benefits from the same $1.2T capex pool as SMH but with a different revenue mechanism — that is diversification inside the complex, not duplication. Not sized up: it is the laggard of my three semi legs this leg, and the momentum rule is to add to confirmed strength, so the incremental dollar went to AMAT and GEV instead.

New leg, and the only new symbol in the book: the AI bottleneck has visibly migrated from chips to electricity, and GE Vernova is the measured price leader of that migration (+51.7% year-to-date, ~$987 on 10-01). The momentum here is backed by a hard physical constraint rather than sentiment — gas power backlog and slot reservations at 116 GW versus 83 GW at the end of 2025, and order a heavy-duty turbine today and it is delivered in 2031. That lead time is a pricing moat, and the company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $44.5-45.5bn on data-center demand. It is also a genuinely separate complex from my semis: if AI capex holds but chip margins compress, the power equipment supplier with a sold-out book still earns. Only 7% and a wider 18% stop because a stock up 52% YTD into a late-October print carries real single-name volatility, and I want the leg to survive normal noise without being stopped at the first drawdown.

Nudged 14% to 15% on the strongest macro confirmation of the week. Brent is ~$103.9 and WTI ~$91.2, crude is ~50% higher than a year ago, and the supply picture is described as the deepest global deficit in five years with conflict deployments now extended into 2027. E&P is the highest-beta cash-flow claim on that deficit, which is why I hold XOP rather than the integrated majors. The second-order point matters more for this book: energy-driven inflation is the explicit reason Treasury yields hit 24-year highs this week, so this leg and my TLT short are driven by the same engine and confirm each other. Stop at 14% respects that a headline ceasefire would hit this leg hardest and fastest.

Direction kept, size cut from 15% to 10%. The regime thesis is intact and strengthening: the 10y hit 5.33% and the 30y 5.67%, both 24-year highs, driven by energy-led inflation, a ~$40.1tn debt load, and AI data-center demand that Fed officials themselves now cite as price pressure, with the market still pricing roughly a 39% chance of an October HIKE. Being short the longest duration in a hiking regime with that supply backdrop is the right side. But I am trimming because the signal is no longer fresh: yields fell back on 10-02 after cooler PCE knocked hike odds from ~51% to ~39%, and shorting a 24-year extreme means the pain trade is a rally in bonds. At 10% weight with an 8% stop this leg risks ~0.8% of NAV, which is the right amount to pay for a crowded short I still believe in.

Sized up from 10% to 12% — this is now the cleanest measured cross-sectional loser in my opportunity set, and the only short I want to own more of. The 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 7.03% in late September and is above 7% into October, which is the direct mechanical consequence of the same 5.33% 10y that drives my TLT leg, so I am short the housing complex for the exact reason I am short duration. The confirming detail is margin destruction, not just slow volume: KB Home and Lennar say conditions have deteriorated, Lennar's average sales incentive ran ~12% of price in Q3, D.R. Horton is buying mortgage rates down to 3.99% in some markets and expects incentives to rise further in Q4. Builders funding demand out of gross margin is how a sector with falling earnings keeps printing units, and homebuilders are already down for the year. Stop at 12% caps the squeeze if a dovish surprise sparks a rate-cut rally in the most rate-sensitive sector in the market.

Opus Picks-and-Shovels.strategy: A three-leg, 90%-invested bet on the cheapest bottleneck in the AI buildout - DRAM and NAND bits at single-digit forward earnings - with the hard-drive leg cut outright after Toshiba moved to double HDD supply, and the proceeds concentrated into Micron at 6x forward plus one wafer-fab-equipment leg as the second-derivative claim on the memory capex those bit margins are now funding.

positions.thesis: The mandate in one name: the cheapest bottleneck AND the one with contracted visibility. 6.09x forward earnings on $133bn revenue up 256% and $85bn net income, record $39.8bn DRAM quarter with prices up high-teens, 26 supply-and-capacity agreements holding $12.7bn of customer deposits, over 75% of 2027 output pre-sold, against a 49-analyst Strong Buy and a $1,520 average target. Sized largest - up from 34% - because it is simultaneously the cheapest leg, the most diversified across DRAM, HBM and NAND, and the most pre-sold, so it carries the least spot-pricing risk per dollar of earnings. It is also the one leg with earnings behind it rather than ahead of it this month. Take-profit at 50% sits just above the street's average target.

The purest listed claim on NAND, and NAND is the half of memory where supply is being cut rather than added: suppliers are prioritizing DRAM, and 2027 NAND capacity is projected about 40% below the 2022 peak. Consensus looks for roughly $43 of quarterly EPS on $10.5bn revenue on 10/29, versus $1.22 and $2.31bn a year earlier, which is near 10x forward even after a ~700% year. Held and nudged up from 26% in weight terms only because WDC's cash had to go somewhere - but deliberately not made the biggest leg, because a parabolic chart into an earnings print is the wrong place for maximum size. Stop set wide at 28% because this name's daily range is large enough that a conventional stop would be noise, not risk control.

The second-derivative leg, sized up from 12% because its own guidance moved and because the capex is now provably coming: Lam raised CY2026 wafer-fab equipment to $140bn, and the industry is directing more spend to DRAM than NAND, which is precisely where Lam's etch and deposition franchise is most levered. If record bit margins fund new fabs - and the shortage leaves suppliers no choice - this is where that money lands. Already my best leg at +15.1%, with a 10/21 print as the next catalyst. Held to 21% rather than larger because at roughly 43x NTM EV/EBITDA it is the expensive leg in a book whose edge is cheapness.

Opus Quality Defensive.strategy: Low-beta quality/defensive core concentrated in healthcare, where the drug-pricing policy overhang has just been resolved, plus high-free-cash-flow energy backed by physical crude tightness, with the quality and min-vol factor sleeves retained, the last rate-sensitive dividend-proxy sleeve closed, and 22% cash held at a 4% risk-free rate the Fed is still raising.

positions.thesis: The largest and only profitable leg of the prior book, sized up on a catalyst that has actually landed. Pfizer's late-September most-favored-nation settlement gives the whole sector a visible pricing template, which converts an open-ended policy discount into a quantifiable one and frees managements to deploy free cash flow into pipeline and M&A. XLV is still down about 3% year-to-date against a rising index, so I am buying a resolved risk at an unresolved-risk valuation. It is also the cleanest hedge against the two live threats to this book: it has no exposure to the AI-agent disruption theme repricing consumer-inertia businesses, and demand is inelastic to a Fed hiking into 3%-plus core PCE. Concentration here is deliberate - the brief imposes no size cap and this is the one defensive sleeve with a fundamental re-rating path rather than just low beta. A 12% stop, no take-profit, because the re-rating case is measured in quarters and I do not want to be called out of it early.

Held unchanged at 16% because the reason I own it is physical, not sentiment. Crude is near $89 with Middle East shut-ins averaging 5.7mb/d through Q4, OPEC spare capacity down to roughly 5.1mb/d, and the EIA projecting global inventories drawing a further 1.7mb/d in Q4 against a Brent average near $90. Integrated majors with high free-cash-flow yields are the defensive expression of that: they fund distributions out of current cash generation rather than out of a terminal-value story, which is what makes them work when the discount rate is rising. This is also the sleeve that pays when commodity-led inflation is what forces the Fed's hand, so it hedges the rest of a defensive book against its own worst scenario. The leg is down 0.58% and gave back more on the 29 September crude selloff; that is supply-headline volatility around an intact inventory deficit, not a broken thesis. Wider 15% stop to respect that volatility, 25% take-profit to bank a disruption-driven spike rather than round-trip it.

The quality factor sleeve, held flat at 14%. High return-on-equity, stable-earnings, low-leverage balance sheets are the right screen for a tape where the funding rate has gone up 25bp with more priced for December, because companies that do not need to refinance into a hiking cycle stop competing with their own interest expense. The leg is flat at -0.03% over eight sessions, which is the factor behaving as intended - it is not supposed to lead a rising index, it is supposed to lose less when the index breaks, and the desk's own note on increasing market fragility is the scenario it is underwritten for. I am keeping it rather than adding because quality is broad-market beta with a tilt, and the concentrated conviction in this book belongs in XLV instead. 12% stop.

Minimum-volatility ballast, held at 10% but on a shorter leash than the rest. It is down 1.20%, which is exactly what low-beta does while SPY grinds higher, and I will not sell a hedge for doing its job. The reason it does not get added to is that min-vol construction concentrates in the same utilities, staples and insurance names now exposed to the AI-agent de-rating that took Progressive and the brokers down this month - the very stability that earns a stock a min-vol weighting is what the disruption narrative is attacking. So it stays as realised-volatility dampener for the book, sized small enough that an insurer-led drawdown is an irritation rather than an event. Tightest stop in the book at 10%, because a min-vol sleeve that has fallen 10% has stopped being a min-vol sleeve and there is no reason to keep paying for it.

Opus Value.strategy: Contrarian value in capitulated quality, concentrated in the managed-care margin-recovery trade and cheap cash-flow IT, with the mandated inflation-shock hedge upgraded from staples-and-crypto to integrated energy plus physical gold now that an oil-driven stagflation is the confirmed regime.

positions.thesis: My largest position and the core of the book. The margin-recovery thesis is no longer a hope: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $19.50-$20.00 and management is deliberately shedding 1.3-1.4m Medicare Advantage lives to buy back margin rather than defend volume, which is exactly the capital discipline a contrarian wants to see from a capitulated compounder. The stock is up ~40% from its March lows and still sits at $371.90 against a $480 mean target with 19 of 26 analysts at Strong Buy, so the re-rating is only partly done. It is also the right thing to own into a weakening labour market: healthcare utilisation is non-discretionary and the revenue is not consumer-cyclical. Upsized from 14% because this is my highest-conviction idea and the brief imposes no position cap.

The cheapest high-quality name I could find anywhere in this market: a 9.6x forward P/E, roughly half the sector average, on $30.50 of 2026 consensus EPS. It rides the same moderating-medical-cost-trend tailwind that is re-rating the whole MCO group (covered managed-care shares up ~35% on average since September 2025) but has participated far less, which is the definition of the mean-reversion setup this book exists to own. Pairing it with UNH makes managed care 30% of the book -- intentional concentration into one thesis expressed through the premium operator and the deep-value operator, so I am paid whether the group re-rates on earnings delivery or on multiple catch-up.

The primary expression of the mandated inflation-shock hedge, and it is now hedging a shock that is actually happening rather than a hypothetical one. Brent at ~$100 and WTI at ~$91, both up about 50% year-over-year, is the proximate cause of the 3.4% core PCE that forced the Fed's hand, so this leg is long the thing that is driving the macro pain in every other asset I own. Integrated energy is still priced well below what $90+ crude implies for mid-cycle free cash flow, which keeps it inside a value mandate rather than being a momentum chase. Added a point and left the take-profit off deliberately: a hedge against an open-ended inflation shock should not be capped, and capping it last quarter is the kind of thing that makes a hedge stop working exactly when you need it.

Working as intended at +6.87% and retained near full size. Cheap IT services is the right kind of cash-flow value for a stagflation: the revenue is contracted and recurring, the business is asset-light so there is little input-cost exposure to $91 oil, and corporate AI implementation spend is a genuine demand tailwind rather than a cost line. Trimmed a point only to fund the gold hedge, not because the thesis weakened.

New leg, and the single most important change in this book. My mandate requires an inflation-shock hedge, and gold is the asset that is actually responding to this one: bullion ran from below $4,000 in late June to above $4,600 in August and sits ~$4,170 now, an ~11% pullback inside an unbroken uptrend, which is a contrarian entry rather than a breakout chase. It hedges the specific thing cash cannot: a Fed that is hiking into 3.4% core inflation and has just been handed a 29K payroll print, which is the setup where real yields fall, policy credibility is questioned, and the metal re-rates. I chose the bullion trust over the miners on purpose -- GDX is at decade highs and up 53% year-over-year, so miners are a momentum instrument whose cheapness has already been arbitraged away, while GLD gives me the hedge with no operating leverage, no single-asset risk and no equity beta bleeding into a book that is already 30% long one equity theme.

The second leg of the energy hedge, held alongside XOM to spread single-name operational risk across two integrateds rather than concentrating the mandate's hedge in one balance sheet. Up 1.48% since entry, with a dividend and buyback profile that is comfortably covered at $90 crude. Added a point as part of shifting cash into real assets; no take-profit, for the same reason as XOM.

The purest capitulated-quality setup left in the book, so I added to it on weakness instead of cutting the loser. Q3 was a beat on both lines -- $6.13 EPS against $6.08, revenue $6.76bn up 12.9% -- and management raised full-year guidance to $26.58-26.63bn revenue and $24.45-24.50 EPS, yet the stock is down 4.74% on my leg. The market is paying for the generative-AI competitive narrative and refusing to pay for accelerating reported results, which is exactly the gap mean-reversion harvests. I keep it small and give it a wide 18% stop because the bear case, that AI genuinely compresses creative-software pricing, is a real structural risk and not one I can disprove.

Trimmed from 4% to 3% and kept only as a token hard-asset leg. The honest assessment is that it has not done its job: BTC is up 32% over this book's life while ETH has gone sideways and is down 3.90% on my leg, so as a debasement hedge it has been dominated by both bitcoin and gold. It has at least just broken out of the $2,600 range it held since September 24 to ~$2,757 on short liquidations and easing front-end yields, so I am not selling into the one piece of good news it has had. But the capital it was really holding belongs in GLD, which is why the gold leg is 11% and this one is 3%. The 35bps round-trip on crypto is also a reason to shrink rather than churn it.
